chapter: Los Angeles: Roy Milton and Central Avenue
title: Billy Berg's club and Slim Gaillard
summary: Billy Berg's club, the Truville, Slim Gaillard's group, and nightly broadcasts with no cover.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Wasn't this about the period when Billy Berg's club was ...(?)

Oh yeah, it was going really strong. It was located there at Longtree(?) and Vine. And he had also owned the Swing Club up on Hollywood Boulevard and Las Palmas, which I played -- later on I will talk about it.
And he had another club that Nat Cole and Lester Young and them used to play before that, before I came there, called the Truville.

Right. And at the club, Slim Gaillard, the great entertainer and musician, he was like a mainstay at Billy Berg's. At that time he had Big Tiny playing the bass. And he'd use the great Leo Watson, who was one of the early scat singers and played drums and trombone. Scatman Crothers also worked with him out there later on.
He worked with Slim at Billy Berg's later on. And I'll tell you when he first came later; to California later...

Billy Berg was quite a man. He really was a nightclub owner. He knew how to do it, you know. He kept great entertainment on his stage. And he kept the broadcasts coming out every night. Every night, whoever was there would broadcast thirty minutes every night. And no cover, no minimum, and everything was just beautiful -- all the bartenders were beautiful... In fact, we used to play on Tuesday nights on the jam sessions, and on Sunday afternoons on the jam sessions. We'd broadcast on Tuesday nights, you know, because I had nights off where I could in there and do
it, see, in the first part of the week there. And oh, we had a lot of... All the fine players used to come through there and play.
